Anchor.description: Identifies which feature output contains the target entity.

oneOf.description: References an output of a specific feature in the tree.
References a datum (construction plane, axis, or point).

AxisDescriptor.description:
The rotation-invariant content of a face on a surface of revolution: what
identifies that face no matter where around the axis you look at it.

**Why a fingerprint needs this** (N0 of `specs/agent_mechanical_design.md`
§5.1). A face that goes all the way round its axis has no distinguished
point: its area-weighted centroid lies ON the axis, where the surface
normal is not defined and the direction from the axis to "the centroid" is
whatever f64 summation rounding left behind — measured at 3.1e-17 m off a
cylinder's axis, so changing that cylinder's height from 2 to 2.0001 swung
the reported centroid 58° round the axis and flipped the reported normal.
A fingerprint exists to be STABLE, so such a face reports no point normal
at all and carries this instead: the axis, the on-axis centroid (in
[`TopoSignature::centroid`], which is a feature — it pins the axial
position), and the surface's own radii.

Every cylinder, cone, sphere and torus face carries one, full turn or not;
it is read straight off the analytic surface, so it is exact either way.
Whether the face ALSO has a point normal is what says where its centroid
is: a face with a normal has its centroid projected onto the surface, a
face without has it on the axis.

direction.description:
Unit axis direction, canonicalised into one half-space so the value
does not depend on which way round the constructor ran the axis.
`None` for a sphere, which has no distinguished axis.

extent.description:
How far this FACE reaches along the axis, in meters — the one field
here that is about the trim rather than the surface, so a short band
and a long one on the same cylinder are told apart. `None` for a
sphere (no axis to measure along).

radius.description:
Distance from the axis: a cylinder's radius, a torus's MAJOR radius, a
sphere's radius. `None` for a cone, whose radius varies along the axis.

DimensionKind.description:
How a dimension measures its anchors.

§7: "`DimensionKind` reuses the seven sketch dimension kinds, with
`Ordinate` added." The seven are the value-bearing arms of
[`crate::sketch::SketchConstraint`] and the names here are deliberately
theirs, so the correspondence is checkable by grep rather than by belief.
The drafting vocabulary a user sees differs: `Distance` is an **aligned**
dimension, `HDistance`/`VDistance` are **linear** horizontal/vertical, and
`Angle` is **angular**. That translation is the UI's.

oneOf.description:
Aligned linear: the distance between two anchors, measured along the
line joining them — or, for two parallel lines, between them.
(`SketchConstraint::Distance`.)

Perpendicular distance from a point to a line.
(`SketchConstraint::PointLineDistance`.)

`|Δu|` only: the horizontal component, leaving the vertical free.
(`SketchConstraint::HDistance`.)
`|Δv|` only. (`SketchConstraint::VDistance`.)
Radius of a circle, arc or ellipse. (`SketchConstraint::Radius`.)

Diameter — twice the radius, drawn through the centre.
(`SketchConstraint::Diameter`.)

One coordinate of a single anchor, measured from the view's ordinate
origin along `axis`. Added by §7; it has no sketch counterpart.
Entity's surface/curve type must match.
Entity's normal must be within `tolerance` radians of `direction`.
Entity must be within `distance` of `point`.
Entity's area must be in range [min, max].

GeomRef.description:
Persistent geometry reference. The core of the persistent naming system.
A GeomRef identifies a specific topological entity across parametric rebuilds.

anchor.description: Which feature's output contains this entity.

kind.description: What kind of topological entity this references.

policy.description: What to do when resolution is ambiguous or fails.

scope.description:
Where the anchor lives when it is NOT in the current tab (v4 §2.8,
in-context editing): the assembly whose instance owns the geometry
and the chain of instance ids down to it. Absent ⇒ local (the current
tab). A reader that does not know this field would silently resolve
the anchor locally, so its arrival bumped the reader floor (format v5).

selector.description: How to find the specific entity within the anchor's output.

Measured.description:
What determines a dimension's value.

Never a number a user typed. See the module docs for why this has three
arms where §7 sketched two.

oneOf.description:
The default: the value is whatever [`measure::measure`] reads off the
anchors' geometry, recomputed every rebuild. Nothing is stored, so
nothing can go stale.

Re-measured every rebuild by evaluating this expression in the
document's parameter environment — which, from D2, includes the
measurement functions (`distance(…)`, `radius(…)`, `mass(…)`). For a
dimension whose number is a *derived* quantity rather than the plain
measurement of its own anchors.

A struct variant, not §7's `Expr(String)` newtype: serde's
internally-tagged representation (`#[serde(tag = "type")]`, which every
persisted enum in this tree uses) cannot serialize a newtype variant
wrapping a primitive — there is nowhere to put the tag. Same for
[`Measured::Value`].

A literal, in meters (radians for an angular dimension).

**Not authorable.** This arm exists for two readers: a nominal
imported from a PMI-bearing file, and a cache written by a build that
wants the last known number available without a kernel. A UI must not
offer it — a typed dimension is how a drawing comes to disagree with
its part.

OrdinateAxis.description: Which view-plane axis an [`DimensionKind::Ordinate`] dimension reads.

oneOf.description: The view's horizontal axis.
The view's vertical axis.

OutputKey.description: Identifies which output of a feature to look in.

oneOf.description: The primary solid body output.
A secondary body (e.g., from boolean split).
A sketch profile (closed loop suitable for extrusion).
A datum plane/axis/point output.

A body a custom feature script named in its return value
(`specs/custom_features_and_modeling_roadmap.md` §A6: `#{ hub: … }`
⇒ `Named { name: "hub" }`). The script's `main` body stays `Main`.

Placement2.description:
The cosmetic offset of a label from its computed position, in view-plane
units (meters, like [`crate::kernel::projection::Curve2`]).

The same idea the sketch dimension labels already have, where the app
keeps it per constraint in `dimensionLabelOffsets`. Zero means "wherever
the layout puts it", which is the only value a freshly authored
annotation has.

RefScope.description:
Scope of a geometry reference into another tab's instance (v4 §2.8).

`source_id` absent ⇒ this document; `tab_id` absent ⇒ the current tab;
`instance_path` = the chain of assembly-instance ids from the referencing
assembly (`tab_id`) down to the part instance whose feature output the
anchor names. A Part feature edited in the context of an assembly
references the OTHER instances this way; the engine resolves such a
reference through its edit context (the `feature_engine::context`
module) and reports it loudly when the context is not open.

instance_path.description: Chain of assembly-instance ids down to the owning part instance.

source_id.description: The document the assembly lives in; absent ⇒ this document.

tab_id.description: The assembly tab the instance path starts from; absent ⇒ the current tab.

ResolvePolicy.description: What to do when GeomRef resolution is ambiguous or fails.

oneOf.description: Fail the rebuild if the reference cannot be uniquely resolved.
Use the closest match and emit a warning.

Role.description:
Semantic role assigned to topological entities by modeling operations.
Roles provide stable, meaningful names for geometry that survive topology changes.

oneOf.description: The face on the positive extrusion direction end.
The face on the negative extrusion direction end (original sketch plane face).
A lateral face created by sweeping a profile edge.
The face at the start of a revolution.
The face at the end of a revolution (if not full 360).
A face created by a fillet operation.
A face created by a chamfer operation.
An inner face created by a shell operation.
The original profile face (sketch plane) of an extrude/revolve.
An instance in a pattern operation.
A face from the first body in a boolean operation.
A face from the second body in a boolean operation.

A face or edge a custom feature script named in its return value
(`#{ hub_face: query }` ⇒ `Named { name: "hub_face" }` on the entity
the query resolved to). Later features select it by name without
knowing the script's private sub-tree.

Selector.description: How to find a specific entity within a feature's output.

oneOf.description: Select by semantic role assigned during the operation.
Select by geometric signature matching.
Select by user-specified geometric query.
Select by 3D position (nearest entity within tolerance).

Select by **persistent id** — the preferred selector for anything
that must stay attached to one specific entity across rebuilds: a
drawing dimension's anchor, a PMI item, an `UpTo` termination, a
3D-sketch attachment (drawings spec D0,
`specs/drawings_and_mbd.md` §4 item 4).

Both ids come from `waffle_types::kernel::EntityPid`. `pid` names the
entity; `root_pid` names where its geometry was introduced, so the
reference still resolves when a later boolean rebuilt the face it
pointed at. For edges and vertices the two are equal — their ids are
content-seeded through the faces' roots already.

Both are `u64` in Rust and **decimal STRINGS on the wire** — in a
`.waffle` file (format v9) and in every message and tool payload
alike. A content-seeded id routinely exceeds `2^53`, where a JSON
number stops being exact in JavaScript; see [`crate::pid_str`] for
the measurement and for why there is one representation rather than
one per boundary. Reading accepts a bare number too, so every file
written before the flip still loads.

Unlike every other selector this one NEVER rebinds: an entity whose
id and root are both gone is a loud `ResolutionFailed`, under either
`ResolvePolicy`. A nearest-match fallback is exactly how an
annotation ends up dimensioning the wrong edge, and the whole point
of a persistent id is that its absence is information.

TieBreak.description: Tie-breaking strategy when multiple entities match a query.

oneOf.description: Pick the entity with the largest area.
Pick the entity nearest to the given point.

Pick the entity whose centroid lies farthest along `direction`
(the top face of a boss: `[0, 0, 1]`). Ties keep the first.
Pick the entity with the smallest index (arbitrary but deterministic).

filters.description: Filters to narrow down candidate entities.

tie_break.description: How to break ties if multiple entities match.

TopoSignature.description:
Geometric signature of a topological entity.
Used for signature-based matching when role-based resolution fails.

axis.description:
The rotation-invariant content of a surface of revolution. Serde-
defaulted: a document written before N0 simply has no key here.

bbox.description: Axis-aligned bounding box [min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z].

centroid.description:
Centroid position [x, y, z]. For a face on a surface of revolution
that goes all the way round, this is the area centroid ON THE AXIS and
`normal` is `None`; a consumer that needs a point on the face itself
must require `normal` alongside it (see [`AxisDescriptor`]).

normal.description:
Outward-pointing normal at centroid (for faces). `None` where there is
no single one: a full-turn surface of revolution, whose centroid lies
on its axis (see [`AxisDescriptor`]).

surface_type.description: Surface type (planar, cylindrical, conical, spherical, toroidal, nurbs).

description:
One annotation on a drawing sheet or in a part's PMI.

`GeomRef` is large (it carries a `TopoSignature`), so every variant that
holds one is large. Same call as [`crate::geom_ref::Selector`] and
feature-engine's `Operation`: a serialized document type, one per
annotation rather than one per vertex, matched and constructed at a
handful of sites. Boxing would ripple through the file format to buy a
smaller discriminant.
`Annotation` is deliberately NOT `PartialEq`: [`GeomRef`] is not, and
making it so means deriving `PartialEq` down through `TopoSignature` and
`TopoQuery` — a change to the reference types several other consumers
share, for the sake of a convenience here. Two annotations are compared by
their serialized form, which is also the form that is persisted and the
only one equality would need to agree with.

oneOf.description: A dimension: how to measure, what to measure, and where the label sits.

anchors.description: The entities measured, in the order [`DimensionKind`] expects.

dual_unit.description:
A second unit shown in brackets beneath the primary one (a unit key
of `app/src/lib/units.js`: `"mm"`, `"in"`, …). `None` ⇒ the
document setting, which may itself be none.

precision.description: Decimal places to show. `None` ⇒ the document setting.

oneOf.description: Free text, optionally with a leader to an entity.
The centre cross of a circular entity.
A centre line between two entities (two parallel walls, two holes).
A datum feature label (`A`, `B`, …) for M1/M2's tolerance frames.
